newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa market pauses to digest crop data.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa market pauses to digest crop data.

text.p: German cocoa consumers were largely inactive as they sought to reconcile differing crop data received this week, traders said on Thursday.
"It's hard to find direction when the ICCO (International Cocoa Organization) sees a surplus of 120,000 tonnes in 1995/96 and (ED&F) Man estimates 36,000 tonnes," one said.
"The market is bound to be confused when it's trying to fit in the forecasts for 96/97 and what it all means for supply.
"At the same time, there is no shortage of spot West African cocoa and that supports consumers inactivity."
Traders said European processors last bought at the end of last week and demand for beans and products had been dormant since then.
The strength of sterling versus the mark also deterred buyers.
The industry was seeen interested in buying December on a 960 stg/tonne basis.
London Dec futures were at 977 at 1400 GMT.
Local bean prices were 2.22 marks/kg for 1996, up 0.02, and 2.27 for first quarter 1997.
The 1996 cocoa butter ratio was steady at 2.83 while the first quarter 1997 ratio was up four points at 2.73.
Implied cocoa butter prices liquid ex-works were 6.38 marks for the fourth quarter and 6.25 for the Jan-March 1997.
